answer.text:
The removal of the operator ID field (OP_ID) from the waste write-off extract was proposed by Priya Nair, Acme's IT Integration Lead, and agreed by Nadia Haddad for RELEX. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]

Chronology: on 24 September 2024, at the master data workshop, Kwame Boateng first noticed an unexpected operator identifier column on some of the movement records, mostly write-offs [T06U0099-T06U0104]. Priya Nair said "We do not need to send you" it, Kwame Boateng said "I do not need to receive it", and Priya Nair proposed "Then let us take it out" [T06U0106-T06U0109]. Ana Duarte asked whether it was a change request; Priya Nair called it "a five minute change" and put it on the list, and Ana Duarte noted it as an action [T06U0113-T06U0119]. This was a proposal and an action, not a confirmed implementation. [6] [7] [8] [9] [10] [11] [1] [12] [13] [14] [15]

On 17 November 2025, at the fresh Phase 2 go/no-go, Priya Nair raised it again as a condition, explaining that the waste write-off records carry the operator item out, so RELEX reading the waste data is also reading who threw what away, per person, per store, per day, and that the works council would ask [T17U0103-T17U0109, T17U0136-T17U0138]. Nadia Haddad said "We do not use that field" but confirmed RELEX receives it [T17U0127-T17U0130]. Priya Nair set exclusion as a condition, not a request [T17U0145]. Nadia Haddad agreed to confirm in writing and to drop it at the extract and exclude it at source [T17U0139, T17U0150-T17U0154]. Lena Fischer said "Good catch, Priya" [T17U0158]. Priya Nair noted it had been in every feed since February [T17U0161-T17U0163]. [16] [17] [18] [19] [20] [21] [22] [23] [24] [2] [25] [3] [4] [26] [27] [28]

On 18 November 2025, Priya Nair confirmed in writing that exclusion was a condition rather than a request, naming the field OP_ID as a six digit operator identifier identifying the individual who scanned the item out, with examples from the November file, and asked what had been done with files already delivered [E07M004]. [29]

On 19 November 2025, Nadia Haddad confirmed OP_ID is dropped at the extract from the next run, which is Friday night, and said Kwame was checking whether the field made it into anything downstream [E07M003]. [5]

On 24 November 2025, Kwame Boateng reported OP_ID was present in the raw landing zone for every daily file since 14 February, not carried into the aggregated waste tables, but present in row-level reconciliation extracts produced in June and September for the data quality review, two of which were emailed as attachments, once to Priya and once to a distribution list of nine people including three at Meridian. He could purge the landing zone but not the attachments [E07M002]. The weekly update recorded "OP_ID field exclusion agreed and confirmed in writing" [R01M007]. [30] [31]

On 11 December 2025, at the fresh cutover call, Kwame Boateng confirmed exclusion at the extract from the twenty-first of November, confirmed in writing to Priya [T18U0067-T18U0069]. [32] [33] [34]

Had it already been sent anywhere by then? Yes. By the time exclusion was agreed (17-19 November 2025), files containing OP_ID had been delivered since February 2025 [E07M004, T17U0163], and row-level reconciliation extracts containing the field had been emailed in June and September 2025, including to a distribution list with three Meridian recipients [E07M002]. The landing zone could be purged; the emailed attachments could not [E07M002]. Note the earlier 2024 workshop action did not result in exclusion at that time; the field remained in every feed until the November 2025 change took effect on 21 November 2025. [29] [28] [30] [33]

citations.quote:
Nadia,

Following Monday's call, confirming this as a condition rather than a request.

The waste write-off extract currently includes OP_ID, a six digit operator identifier
identifying the individual who scanned the item out. Examples from the November file:

447102  Marika Lindqvist, store 118 Vantaa, nights
448933  Osman Yildirim, store 118 Vantaa
451207  Heidi Salminen, store 094 Espoo

This has been in every file since February. It must be excluded at source before the
next extract runs. Please confirm the field is dropped and tell me what you have done
with the files already delivered.

Our works council will ask. I would rather answer them than be asked.

If the answer to the second question is complicated, put it on the agenda for the
January session rather than replying to this.
citations.title: OP_ID field - exclusion from fresh feed
citations.author: Priya Nair

citations.quote:
Answer on the historic files.

OP_ID is present in the raw landing zone for every daily file since 14 February. It is
not carried into the aggregated waste tables, which group by store and article.

However it is present in the reconciliation extracts we produced in June and September
for the data quality review, because those were row level. Two of those were emailed as
attachments, once to Priya and once to a distribution list of nine people including
three at Meridian.

I can purge the landing zone. I cannot purge the attachments.
